goal: Prevent flow initialization and preparation from deleting or modifying unrelated unresolved preparing-flow records, while retaining target-only deletion after successful conversion.

analysis.problem: The init and prepare paths perform global age-based cleanup of preparing-flow records, and prepare removes its target before conversion completes. This permits unrelated or failed target state to be lost without an explicit, auditable deletion request.
analysis.proposedApproach: Remove age-based global preparing-record deletion from init and prepare, preserve existing store ownership boundaries, and move target deletion to the successful end of preparation conversion.
analysis.validation: Verify byte-identical preservation of unrelated records across init and successful prepare, preservation of target and unrelated records on each prepare failure boundary, target-only removal after success, and absence of reachable TTL-based pruning from these commands.

knownFacts: must: flow set init creates a preparing record and currently globally prunes records older than one hour.
must: flow prepare currently performs global stale cleanup and deletes its selected preparing record before worktree, spec, and active-flow conversion finish.
must: Issue #433 requires unrelated preparing records to remain byte-identical regardless of elapsed time.
must: Issue #433 explicitly excludes reconstruction of the missing #415 record and creation of cleanup or archive operations.
decisionPoints: must: retain existing init and prepare public behavior except for removal of implicit stale deletion.
must: delete only the selected preparing record and only after successful conversion.
must: replace TTL-deletion expectations with preservation, isolation, and failure-atomicity coverage.
resolvedByProjectRules: must: preserve existing FlowStore and preparing-store ownership boundaries rather than adding a parallel state-management path.
must: use Node.js built-in modules only and add no compatibility shim.
deferredToSpec: must: enumerate the concrete validation, agent, write, and conversion failure seams covered by focused tests.
must: map each obsolete TTL assertion to a preservation or non-pruning assertion.

in: must: make flow set init list or warn about existing preparing runs without deleting or modifying them.
must: make successful flow prepare remove only its selected preparing run after conversion succeeds.
must: preserve selected and unrelated preparing runs unchanged when prepare fails.
must: remove or make unreachable global TTL pruning used by init and prepare.
must: replace obsolete one-hour and 61-minute deletion tests with byte-preservation, isolation, and failure-atomicity tests.
out: must: do not reconstruct, infer, or silently replace the missing #415 preparing record.
must: do not design or add cleanup, archive, or audited deletion commands.
must: do not change unrelated flow lifecycle behavior or add dependencies or public compatibility shims.

impactOnExisting: must: unresolved preparing runs older than one hour remain available instead of being implicitly deleted by init or prepare.
must: init retains its creation result and existing-run warning behavior, with warning membership including all unresolved runs rather than only fresh runs.
must: successful prepare still converts its selected preparing run into active spec state and removes that selected source record.
must: failed prepare now preserves retryable preparing state rather than losing the selected record.
must: no other public init or prepare output or command contract changes.

qa.question: must: Should the fix preserve every unrelated unresolved preparing-flow record byte-identically across both init and prepare, regardless of record age?
qa.answer: must: Yes. Unrelated unresolved preparing-flow records remain byte-identical across init and prepare regardless of elapsed time.
qa.evidence: Issue #433 acceptance criteria explicitly require byte-identical preservation of stale run A across init B and successful prepare B.
qa.why: must: Elapsed time alone is not an explicit, target-guarded, or auditable instruction to destroy unresolved state.
qa.considered: Retaining the one-hour prune was rejected because it caused the unrelated #415 loss and violates the published data-integrity invariant.

qa.question: must: Should prepare remove only its selected preparing-flow record, and only after all conversion work has succeeded?
qa.answer: must: Yes. Successful prepare deletes only its selected record after conversion succeeds.
qa.evidence: Issue #433 requires target-record deletion only after successful conversion; src/flow/lib/run-prepare-spec.js currently deletes the target before worktree, spec, and flow-state creation.
qa.why: must: Post-conversion deletion makes the preparing record the retryable source until its replacement state exists successfully.
qa.considered: Pre-conversion deletion was rejected because later validation, agent, write, or conversion failure would destroy retry state.

qa.question: must: Should failed prepare attempts leave both the selected and unrelated preparing-flow records unchanged at validation, agent, write, and conversion failure boundaries?
qa.answer: must: Yes. Both selected and unrelated preparing records remain unchanged whenever prepare fails.
qa.evidence: Issue #433 requirements and verification explicitly name validation, agent, write, and conversion failures and require both A and B to remain unchanged.
qa.why: must: Failure atomicity prevents partial preparation from silently consuming the only unresolved request state.
qa.considered: Preserving only unrelated records was rejected because it would still lose the selected record on a retryable failure.

qa.question: must: Should public init and prepare behavior remain unchanged except that unresolved preparing records are no longer deleted solely because of elapsed time?
qa.answer: must: Yes. The public contract remains unchanged except for removal of implicit age-based deletion.
qa.evidence: Issue #433 acceptance criteria require public init and prepare behavior to stay unchanged except for removing stale global deletion.
qa.why: must: The bug fix remains minimal and does not broaden into unrelated lifecycle changes.
qa.considered: Changing warnings, target selection, or preparation output was rejected as outside the published scope.

qa.question: must: Should this fix exclude reconstruction of #415 and any new cleanup, archive, or audited deletion design?
qa.answer: must: Yes. Do not reconstruct #415 and do not add cleanup, archive, or audited deletion design.
qa.evidence: Issue #433 lists all of these as explicit non-goals and states the missing record cannot be recovered exactly without a tombstone or journal.
qa.why: must: Inventing lost state or a new lifecycle operation would exceed the minimal prevention fix and could create additional data-integrity risk.
qa.considered: Inferred reconstruction and implicit replacement cleanup were rejected because neither can preserve exact historical state or provide an explicit deletion audit trail.

approval.notes: Published Issue #433 resolves every draft decision; no unresolved user-decision item remains.
